symbols.name: S2
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak S_2=\{\mathrm{id},\mathrm{sw}\}\) acts simultaneously on every coordinate indexed by \(z\)

symbols.name: Theta_eta
symbols.role: proposal-specific compact box for all mixing, assignment, and transition primitives

symbols.name: sigma_psi
symbols.def: For \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_2\), \(\sigma\psi\) replaces every type-indexed coordinate \(q_z\) of \(\psi\) by \(q_{\sigma^{-1}(z)}\), including \(\pi_z,e_z,u_{zd},a_{zi},b_{ztj},c_{ztj}\)
symbols.role: simultaneous relabeling of a structural representation

symbols.name: M_eta
symbols.role: independently stated fixed compact-interior latent-transition model

symbols.name: tilde_Phi
symbols.role: all labeled structural representations of the observed law

symbols.name: bar_tau
symbols.role: ATT induced on simultaneous-label equivalence classes

symbols.name: v
symbols.def: \(v=(v_{zdk})_{z\in\{1,2\},\ d,k\in\mathcal A}\) is a free terminal-transition coordinate of a lifted chart
symbols.role: generic terminal coordinate before structural reconstruction

symbols.name: c
symbols.role: index of one of sixteen terminal charts

symbols.name: R
symbols.def: \(R=(R_{zd}(i,j,k))_{z\in\{1,2\},\ d,i,j,k\in\mathcal A}\) is a free lifted-chart coordinate and is not a conditional table of the observed law \(P\)
symbols.role: generic latent prefix coordinate before structural reconstruction

symbols.name: R_psi
symbols.def: For \(\psi\in\Theta_\eta\), \(R(\psi)_{zd}(i,j,k)=\Pr_{\psi}(Z=z,X_1=i,X_2=j,X_3=k\mid D=d)\); this table belongs to the structural law indexed by \(\psi\), not to the observed law \(P\)
symbols.role: structural latent table mapped into a lifted chart

symbols.name: v_psi
symbols.role: structural terminal table mapped into a lifted chart

symbols.name: Xchart
symbols.def: \(\mathsf X=\mathbb R^{32}\times\mathbb R^8\) with generic point \(x=(R,v)\)
symbols.role: common ambient space for latent-prefix and terminal coordinates

symbols.name: X_c
symbols.def: \(\mathsf X_c=\{(R,v)\in\mathsf X:v_{1dk}=v_{2dk}\text{ if }c_{dk}=1,\ v_{1dk}\ne v_{2dk}\text{ if }c_{dk}=0\}\)
symbols.role: lifted space for one exact terminal-collision pattern

symbols.name: Gamma_c
symbols.def: \(\Gamma_c(P)\subseteq\mathsf X_c\) is the set of chart points \(x=(R,v)\) satisfying terminal splitting against \(H(P),N(P)\), the eight equations \(\rho_{zdj}(R)=0\), the four equations \(\gamma_{zi}(R)=0\), and every reconstructed \(\eta\)-box inequality
symbols.role: semialgebraic subset of the lifted collision-pattern space

symbols.name: rec_c
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{rec}_c(P,x)\) is obtained from \(x=(R,v)\) by the displayed positive-mass ratios for \(w_{zd},u_{zd},a_{zi},\kappa_{zd3j},\pi_z,e_z\), with terminal row \(\kappa_{zd4k}=v_{zdk}\)
symbols.role: map from a lifted feasible point to a labeled structural representation

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: \(V\subset\mathcal M_\eta\) denotes a relative neighborhood of \(P\)
symbols.role: law domain of a branch-continuity parameterization

symbols.name: K_c
symbols.def: \(K_c\) denotes a fixed compact parameter set indexed by chart \(c\)

symbols.name: g_c
symbols.def: \(g_c(P',k)\) denotes a continuous semialgebraic parameterization whose image in \(k\) is \(\Gamma_c(P')\)
symbols.role: lifted chart parameterization, never a structural representation map

symbols.name: chi
symbols.def: For \(d,k,i,j\in\mathcal A\), \(\chi_{dk}^{ij}(P)=N_d(i,j,k)H_d(0,0,k)-N_d(0,0,k)H_d(i,j,k)\); vanishing for all \((i,j)\ne(0,0)\) is necessary and sufficient for the observed block to admit a collided-terminal splitting
symbols.role: observable compatibility list for a collided representation chart

symbols.name: Omega_one
symbols.def: \(\Omega_{1\mathrm c}(P,\eta)\) is the sign vector of the explicit collision, rank, alignment, box, and signed-subresultant list in \(\mathrm{def:one-collision-sign-list}\)

symbols.name: Phi_one
symbols.def: \(\widetilde\Phi_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)=\bigcup_{\sigma\in\Sigma}\{\operatorname{rec}_c(P,x):x\in\Gamma_c(P)\text{ satisfies the }\sigma\text{-alignment equations}\}\subseteq\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\), where \(c_{0k_0}=1\) and the other three terminal rows are distinct
symbols.role: early-kill portion of the unquotiented structural fiber

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: \(\Omega(P)=(\operatorname{sgn} g_r(P,\eta))_{r=1}^{K}\), with the finite polynomial list \(\{g_r\}_{r=1}^{K}\) derived by Open-ended Question 1

symbols.name: Alg
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{AtlasATT}(P,\eta)\) takes the reduced binary encodings of the rational numbers \(\eta\) and \(P_{ijkld}\), runs the fixed chartwise elimination schedule in Definition \(\mathrm{def:atlas-algorithm}\), and returns exact semialgebraic and real-algebraic encodings of the identified regions, endpoint witnesses, and branch certificates
symbols.role: constructive exact algorithm for the fixed binary model

symbols.name: BC
symbols.def: \(\mathrm{BC}(P)\) holds when there are a relative neighborhood \(V\subset\mathcal M_\eta\), fixed compact sets \(K_c\), and continuous semialgebraic maps \(g_c:V\times K_c\to\mathsf X_c\) such that \(\Gamma_c(P')=g_c(P',K_c)=\{g_c(P',k):k\in K_c\}\) for every \(P'\in V\), the nonempty-chart inventory is constant on \(V\), every \(\operatorname{rec}_c(P',\cdot)\) is continuous on \(\Gamma_c(P')\), and distinct sets \(\{\tau(\operatorname{rec}_c(P',x);P'):x\in\Gamma_c(P')\}\) have a positive gap on \(V\)

symbols.name: psi_star
symbols.role: reproducible primitive generator of the merger benchmark

symbols.name: P_star
symbols.def: \(P^\star=F(\psi^\star)\); equivalently, all \(32\) cells are \(P^\star_{ijkld}=2^{-1}B(1/2;i)B(3/10+i/2;j)B((1-d)(3/10+j/2)+d/2;k)B((1-d)(3/10+k/2)+d(3/8+j/4);l)\). In particular, \(P^\star(D=1)=1/2\), the common pretransition is \((3/10,4/5)\), both control post-transitions have row \((3/10,4/5)\), treated \(X_3\) is conditionally fair, and the treated date \(4\) success probability is \(3/8+j/4\).

symbols.name: psi_star_end
symbols.role: attaining witnesses for both marginal endpoints of the benchmark law

novel.justification: This proposal-specific compact-interior condition is satisfied by any structural law whose mixing, treatment-assignment, and transition probabilities are strictly interior after choosing a rational \(\eta\) below their minimum distance to zero and one. Rational \(\eta\) supports finite exact chart certification, and the resulting common compact box yields attainment and a fixed domain for the stated uniform procedures. This condition is not inherited from Ahn--Kasahara or from their CS-LT condition.

The first-order Markov and transition-independence parameterization uses the same economic objects as Ahn--Kasahara, but \(\mathcal M_\eta\) is an independently stated model: it places the mixing probability, every conditional treatment-assignment probability, and every conditional transition probability in \([\eta,1-\eta]\). Ahn--Kasahara's CS-LT condition bounds only conditional treatment assignment away from zero and one. The compactification is credible when latent shares and transition rows are not nearly deterministic and is maintained to make every sharp region attained, every exact chart certificate finite, and the uniform procedures live on one fixed compact domain. No inclusion relation between \(\mathcal M_\eta\) and the full published CS-LT class is maintained.

The condition is satisfied on any relatively open sign stratum where the lifted chart domains are fixed compact polytopes, chart discriminants do not vanish, and target components remain separated; these are empirically checkable configurations away from mergers of feasible branches.

definitions.name: Proposal-specific compactly boxed latent-transition law class
Labeled and quotient global transition-alignment fibers
definitions.construction: \(\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)=\{\psi\in\Theta_\eta:F(\psi)=P\}\) and \(\Phi_\eta(P)=\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)/\mathfrak S_2\), where \(\mathfrak S_2\) acts by simultaneous type permutation

definitions.name: Lifted terminal-collision chart spaces
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf X=\mathbb R^{32}\times\mathbb R^8\) with \(x=(R,v)\), and \(\mathsf X_c=\{x\in\mathsf X:v_{1dk}=v_{2dk}\text{ exactly for blocks with }c_{dk}=1\}\); the feasible set \(\Gamma_c(P)\) is a subset of \(\mathsf X_c\)

definitions.name: Sixteen terminal-collision charts
definitions.construction: For each \(c\in\{0,1\}^{4}\), work in \(\mathsf X_c\subset\mathsf X=\mathbb R^{32}\times\mathbb R^8\) with \(x=(R,v)\). For block \((d,k)\), if \(c_{dk}=0\), set \(R_{1d}(i,j,k)=[N_d(i,j,k)-v_{2dk}H_d(i,j,k)]/(v_{1dk}-v_{2dk})\) and \(R_{2d}=H_d-R_{1d}\); if \(c_{dk}=1\), impose \(v_{1dk}=v_{2dk}=v_{dk}\), \(N_d(i,j,k)=v_{dk}H_d(i,j,k)\), retain \(R_{1d}(i,j,k)\) as splitting coordinates, and set \(R_{2d}=H_d-R_{1d}\). Define \(\Gamma_c(P)\subseteq\mathsf X_c\) by these equations, \(\rho_{zdj}(R)=0\), \(\gamma_{zi}(R)=0\), and every reconstructed \(\eta\)-box inequality. For \(x\in\Gamma_c(P)\), define \(\operatorname{rec}_c(P,x)\) by \(w_{zd}=\sum_iS_{zd}^{R}(i)\), \(u_{zd}=S_{zd}^{R}(1)/w_{zd}\), \(a_{zi}=T_{zd}^{R}(i,1)/S_{zd}^{R}(i)\), \(\kappa_{zd3j}=R_{zd}(0,j,1)/T_{zd}^{R}(0,j)\), \(\kappa_{zd4k}=v_{zdk}\), \(\pi_z=p_0w_{z0}+p_1w_{z1}\), and \(e_z=p_1w_{z1}/\pi_z\).

definitions.name: Explicit one-collided-control-row sign list
definitions.construction: Fix \(k_0\in\mathcal A\), set \(c_{0k_0}=1\) and \(c_{0,1-k_0}=c_{10}=c_{11}=0\), and treat \(\sigma\in\Sigma\) separately. The observable vanishing list begins with \(\chi_{0k_0}^{ij}=0\) for \((i,j)\in\{(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}\); set \(v_{10k_0}=v_{20k_0}=N_0(0,0,k_0)/H_0(0,0,k_0)\) and require the two signs \(N_0(0,0,k_0)-\eta H_0(0,0,k_0)\ge0\) and \(UH_0(0,0,k_0)-N_0(0,0,k_0)\ge0\). For the other three blocks enumerate the eight orientation signs \(s_{dk}(v_{1dk}-v_{2dk})>0\), \(s_{dk}\in\{-1,1\}\), and substitute the displayed terminal-splitting formula. Retain \(r_{ij}=R_{10}(i,j,k_0)\). In the fixed variable order \(y=(v_{11,0},v_{21,0},v_{11,1},v_{21,1},v_{10,1-k_0},v_{20,1-k_0},r_{00},r_{01},r_{10},r_{11})\), the equality list is exactly the eight cleared numerators of \(\rho_{zdj}(R)\) and the four cleared numerators of \(\gamma_{zi}(R)\), with control labels replaced by \(\sigma(z)\). The inequality list is exactly the orientation signs, every \(R_{zd}(i,j,k)\ge\eta^5\), and the two cleared numerator signs \(q-\eta\ge0\), \(U-q\ge0\) for each reconstructed \(q\in\{v_{zdk},u_{zd},a_{zi},\kappa_{zd3j},\pi_z,e_z\}\); all clearing denominators are the positive masses \(H_d,T_{zd}^{R},S_{zd}^{R},w_{zd},p_d\) and the signed terminal differences. For a finite polynomial family \(\mathcal F\), define \(\Pi_y(\mathcal F)\) recursively, in the displayed order, by adjoining every coefficient in the current variable, every leading coefficient, every discriminant, every pairwise resultant, and the signed principal subresultant coefficients of each equality with each inequality boundary, then deleting the current variable. The actual observable list \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}\) is the three \(\chi\)'s, the two collided-row box polynomials, and \(\Pi_y\) applied to the twelve equalities and the displayed finite inequality list. Its acceptance rule is signed Sturm--Habicht lifting: retain precisely the real root cells on which the twelve equalities vanish and every listed weak or strict sign holds. Target constancy introduces auxiliary indeterminates \(\lambda_t\), adds the same principal-subresultant list for the cleared numerators of \(\tau_t(\operatorname{rec}_c(P,x);P)-\lambda_t\), \(t\in\{3,4\}\), and accepts exactly when the two reconstructed target coordinates have one common algebraic value on all retained cells. This is a fixed model-specific finite list for each of \(k_0=0,1\) and both \(\sigma=\mathrm{id},\mathrm{sw}\); it is not an invocation of unrestricted multivariate quantifier elimination.

definitions.name: Observable singleton-certificate handle
definitions.construction: Handle: extend the signed-subresultant construction of \(\mathrm{def:one-collision-sign-list}\) chart by chart in the lifted spaces \(\mathsf X_c\). Use each \(\rho_{zdj}(R)=0\) to split proportional-row and rank-zero alternatives, use \(\gamma_{zi}(R)=0\) to retain every feasible cross-arm alignment, and add every reconstructed box numerator before signed Sturm--Habicht lifting. The output is a finite observable polynomial list \(\{g_r(P,\eta)\}_{r=1}^{K}\) whose sign vector determines chart feasibility and whether, for every feasible \(c,c'\) and all \(x\in\Gamma_c(P)\), \(x'\in\Gamma_{c'}(P)\), one has \(\tau(\operatorname{rec}_c(P,x);P)=\tau(\operatorname{rec}_{c'}(P,x');P)\).

definitions.name: Branch-aware exact ATT algorithm
definitions.construction: Encode the input as the reduced signed-binary numerator and positive denominator of \(\eta\) and of each of the \(32\) rational cells \(P_{ijkld}\). Enumerate the sixteen collision patterns \(c\in\{0,1\}^{4}\), grouped by collision count as \(1+4+6+4+1\); refine a pattern having \(r\) collided blocks into \(2^{4-r}\) orientations of its noncollided terminal differences, producing \(\sum_{r=0}^{4}\binom{4}{r}2^{4-r}=81\) collision-orientation cells; and retain both \(\sigma\in\{\mathrm{id},\mathrm{sw}\}\), producing exactly \(162\) base branches. For each base branch build \(\Gamma_c(P)\) by terminal splitting, keep all eight rank-one equations as cleared polynomial equalities, clear only denominators whose signs are recorded, adjoin every reconstructed box numerator, and project in the fixed order terminal rows, prefix splits, arm weights, and relative alignment by signed subresultants and Sturm--Habicht lifting. Vanishing rank coefficients and box faces are retained as zero or weak-sign cells of this lifting and create no additional base branch. Discard a branch only with its violated sign or exact polynomial certificate, isolate every final univariate real root, apply \(\operatorname{rec}_c(P,\cdot)\) to every retained chart point and then evaluate \(\tau\) on each retained compact connected cell, and merge only intersecting images. Encode the joint output by a quantifier-free Boolean combination of integer-polynomial sign conditions in \((\tau_3,\tau_4)\); encode each marginal endpoint by a square-free integer polynomial, a rational isolating interval, and a Thom sign sequence; encode every endpoint witness coordinate in the same real-algebraic format together with its chart, orientation, rank, and alignment labels; and return the exact finite ordered unions and every discarded-branch certificate.

definitions.name: Full-PMF confidence inversion
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_n^P=\{Q\in\Delta_{31}:\lVert Q-\widehat P_n\rVert_\infty\le\delta_n(\alpha)\}\) and \(\mathcal C_n^\tau=\{\tau(\psi;Q):\psi\in\Theta_\eta,\ F(\psi)=Q,\ Q\in\mathcal C_n^P\}\)

statements.statement: For any \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\) and any labeled representation \(\psi\in\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\), the structural coordinate \(x(\psi)=(R(\psi),v(\psi))\) belongs to exactly one \(\mathsf X_c\) and lies in \(\Gamma_c(P)\). Its coordinates satisfy all eight equations \(\rho_{zdj}(R)=0\), all four equations \(\gamma_{zi}(R)=0\), and every reconstructed \(\eta\)-box inequality. Conversely, every \(x\in\Gamma_c(P)\) reconstructs \(\operatorname{rec}_c(P,x)\in\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\), and \(R(\operatorname{rec}_c(P,x))=R\) and \(v(\operatorname{rec}_c(P,x))=v\).
statements.justification: This is the algebraic equivalence that prevents omitted collision, rank-loss, alignment, or boundary branches.
statements.gap: Ahn--Kasahara Proposition 4 under RSM, M, and ID and Higgins--Jochmans Theorem 1 invert regular matrix products; Critch sends denominator-zero observations to lower-dimensional submodels. The chart theorem instead solves two-arm singular reconstruction inside the independently stated all-primitive compact model \(\mathcal M_\eta\). It complements those regular results and makes no claim on the unboxed published class.
statements.consumer: The public \(ak\) package can use the lemma to certify that its fiber search has not silently discarded a merger representation.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\), every \(\psi\in\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\), and every simultaneous type permutation \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_2\), one has \(\sigma\psi\in\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\) and \(\tau(\sigma\psi;P)=\tau(\psi;P)\). Therefore \(\bar\tau_P([\psi])=\tau(\psi;P)\) is a well-defined map on \(\Phi_\eta(P)\).
statements.justification: The identified set is meaningful on quotient classes only after the causal functional is shown invariant to simultaneous type relabeling.
statements.gap: Regular mixture arguments often state recovery only up to labels; this lemma records the exact invariance needed before projecting a singular transition-alignment quotient to aggregate ATT.
statements.consumer: Every chartwise ATT value and endpoint witness can be reported independently of the arbitrary latent-type names used by software.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\), \(\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)=\bigcup_{c\in\{0,1\}^{4}}\operatorname{rec}_c(P,\Gamma_c(P))\). Consequently, \(\Phi_\eta(P)\) is exactly the quotient by simultaneous type permutation of that reconstructed union. These equalities hold at terminal collisions, rank failures, coincident components, all \(\eta\)-box faces, and every feasible relative cross-arm alignment.
statements.justification: A complete fiber atlas is the prerequisite for sharp bounds and point-identification claims at mergers.
statements.gap: Generic tensor and spectral arguments establish recovery away from exceptional sets but do not classify the exceptional transition-alignment fiber.
statements.consumer: Applied users in the Dodd--Frank and Norwegian patent analyses obtain a certified list of all observationally compatible counterfactual transition laws.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\), each \(\mathcal I_t(P)\), \(t\in\{3,4\}\), is a nonempty finite union of compact intervals with attained endpoints. There exists a relatively open subset of a named cross-arm alignment stratum on which each arm is separately recoverable up to labels while \(\mathcal I_t(P)\) has at least two separated components.
statements.justification: The first clause fixes the correct computational object, while the second rules out interval-hull reporting as a generically harmless simplification.
statements.gap: General semialgebraic topology gives finite components but does not supply the causal alignment stratum or prove disconnected ATT images there.
statements.consumer: Set-valued reporting in \(ak\) retains sign-relevant gaps that an interval hull would falsely fill.

statements.statement: There is a positive-dimensional family of pairs \((P,P')\in\mathcal M_\eta^2\) with identical univariate and all six pairwise path marginals in both treatment arms but \(\mathcal I(P)\ne\mathcal I(P')\). The family contains laws with a positive eigenvalue collision and remains nondegenerate under relative perturbations preserving the pair-marginal equalities.
statements.justification: It establishes that the full path tensor is information, not merely a convenient proof device.
statements.gap: Short-trail reconstruction results concern component recovery under nondegeneracy and do not prove ATT-fiber insufficiency of all pair marginals in the coupled-arm model.
statements.consumer: Researchers learn which empirical moment reductions can reverse or erase the aggregate ATT sign region.

statements.statement: For \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\) and \(k_0\in\mathcal A\), the labeled subfiber \(\widetilde\Phi_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) with both treated terminal rows distinct, control row \(k_0\) collided, and control row \(1-k_0\) distinct is exactly the union of \(\operatorname{rec}_c(P,\cdot)\) applied to the accepted signed Sturm--Habicht lifts for \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\mathrm{id}}\) and \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\mathrm{sw}}\). For each \(\sigma\in\{\mathrm{id},\mathrm{sw}\}\), its lift is nonempty if and only if the three collision equalities, the three noncollision orientation alternatives, all eight rank-one equalities, all four \(\sigma\)-alignment equalities, and every displayed box sign in \(\mathrm{def:one-collision-sign-list}\) accept a common root cell. Its quotient ATT image is a singleton if and only if every nonempty lift has zero coordinatewise target oscillation after reconstruction and the two relative-alignment values coincide. Otherwise the retained cells reconstruct two labeled feasible representations with distinct ATT vectors and their exact scalar images give the attained marginal subregions. These conditions are necessary and sufficient even when a rank coefficient vanishes or a primitive lies on an \(\eta\)-box face.
statements.justification: This completes the mandated destructive subcase with an explicit observable list, both relative alignments, rank-zero branches, and all box contacts before the remaining fourteen chart patterns are attempted.
statements.gap: Ahn--Kasahara Proposition 4 identifies parameters under RSM, M, and ID, while no cited algebraic-mixture result supplies this one-collided-row causal classification under TI-LT. Their CS-LT condition bounds only conditional treatment assignment. This theorem is a new-condition result inside the independently compactified \(\mathcal M_\eta\), not a claim about their unboxed singular class.
statements.consumer: The branch engine of the public \(ak\) package receives a finite acceptance table for the first singular configuration that defeats the regular eigendecomposition.

statements.statement: Extend the finite model-specific polynomial family \(\{g_r(P,\eta)\}_{r=1}^{K}\) in \(\mathrm{def:singleton-certificate-handle}\) from the completed one-collided-control-row list to all sixteen \(\Gamma_c(P)\). Prove that its sign vector determines feasibility of every lifted chart and whether, for every pair of feasible charts \(c,c'\), every \(x\in\Gamma_c(P)\), and every \(x'\in\Gamma_{c'}(P)\), \(\tau(\operatorname{rec}_c(P,x);P)=\tau(\operatorname{rec}_{c'}(P,x');P)\), including all multiple-collision and coincident-component rank deficiencies, without invoking unrestricted multivariate quantifier elimination.
statements.justification: This is the irreducible open content after the early-kill stratum: an observable necessary-and-sufficient point-identification criterion on every remaining exceptional fiber.
statements.gap: Ahn--Kasahara Proposition 4 and Proposition 5 plus Corollary 1 identify the regular model and ATT under RSM, M, TI-LT, and ID, while generic algebraic identifiability results leave the exceptional set unclassified. The finite exact atlas is asked only on the independently stated \(\mathcal M_\eta\), which boxes every mixing, assignment, and transition primitive; it does not promise a result on the published unboxed singular class.
statements.consumer: The criterion tells an applied analyst whether a reported aggregate ATT sign is a feature of the observed law or of a selected latent decomposition.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\), \(\mathcal I(P)\) is a singleton if and only if, for all feasible charts \(c,c'\), all \(x\in\Gamma_c(P)\), and all \(x'\in\Gamma_{c'}(P)\), \(\tau(\operatorname{rec}_c(P,x);P)=\tau(\operatorname{rec}_{c'}(P,x');P)\). Equivalently, \(\Omega(P)\) belongs to the finite acceptance set delivered by Open-ended Question 1. If the sign vector is rejected, the same certificate returns two reconstructed labeled representations with distinct values of \((\tau_3,\tau_4)\).
statements.justification: Both sufficiency and counter-witness necessity convert regular identification into an exact observable frontier.
statements.gap: No cited paper gives necessary and sufficient observable conditions for a causal functional to remain constant across every singular arm-aligned mixture representation.
statements.consumer: Dodd--Frank, patenting, and ADA specifications receive a reproducible point-versus-partial identification diagnostic.

statements.statement: For rational \(\eta\) and rational \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\), supplied as the reduced binary encodings of \(\eta\) and all \(32\) cells \(P_{ijkld}\), \(\mathsf{AtlasATT}(P,\eta)\) examines exactly sixteen terminal-collision patterns, \(81\) collision-orientation cells, and \(162\) relative-alignment base branches. Rank-coefficient zeros and box contacts are sign cells inside those branches, not omitted denominator cases. Every base branch follows the fixed finite projection order in \(\mathrm{def:atlas-algorithm}\), so the procedure terminates after finitely many signed-subresultant and univariate root-isolation operations. It returns exactly the attained joint set \(\mathcal I(P)\) as an integer-polynomial sign formula, each marginal \(\mathcal I_t(P)\) as a finite ordered union of closed intervals with real-algebraic endpoint encodings, a real-algebraic feasible representation with branch labels for every endpoint and isolated component, and an exact sign or polynomial infeasibility certificate for every discarded branch.
statements.justification: The fixed binary inventory, rational input convention, exact output convention, and \(162\)-base-branch count make termination and auditability part of the theorem rather than an implementation promise.
statements.gap: Duarte and coauthors give general spatial branch-and-bound with \(\epsilon\)-sharpness, while Henry--Kitamura--Salanie characterize a different exact mixture set under excluded weight variation; neither gives this fixed-model finite branch count, exact finite-union encoding, or latent endpoint witnesses.
statements.consumer: The \(ak\) package obtains auditable exact benchmarks and a branch-aware numerical implementation for merger fits.

statements.statement: The complete rational primitive \(\psi^\star\) belongs to \(\Theta_\eta\) for every rational \(0<\eta<3/20\), so \(P^\star=F(\psi^\star)\in\mathcal M_\eta\) and its displayed formula fixes all \(32\) observed cells, including \(P^\star(D=1)=1/2\). At \(\eta=1/10\), \(\mathcal I_3(P^\star)=[-8867/29480,7517/29480]\) and \(\mathcal I_4(P^\star)=[-8611/29480,7773/29480]\). Every unequal-ATT representation has common prehistory, the control arm lies in exactly four convex decomposition cases, and the four fully specified representations \(\psi_{3,h}^\star,\psi_{4,h}^\star\), \(h\in\{1/10,9/10\}\), all satisfy \(F(\psi_{t,h}^\star)=P^\star\) and attain the two endpoints of the corresponding \(\mathcal I_t(P^\star)\). At \(\eta=7/50\), a probability-box face in the one-collided-terminal control case changes the date-\(4\) extremizing branch.
statements.justification: The exact merger law is a destructive benchmark for missed branches, false sign conclusions, and probability-box phase switches.
statements.gap: No published calculation gives full sharp ATT regions for this singular binary four-period latent-transition law; the result is supporting evidence rather than the general kernel.
statements.consumer: Package tests can compare every endpoint and witness using rational arithmetic before deployment on empirical applications.

statements.statement: Let \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\) also satisfy Ahn--Kasahara's Assumptions RSM and M, their Assumption TI-LT linking latent transition types to the causal path, and their Assumption ID requiring regular nonsingularity, distinct eigenvalues, and alignment. On this regular intersection, their Proposition 4 identifies the parameter vector, Proposition 5 identifies LTATT, and Corollary 1 identifies aggregate ATT, and \(\mathsf{AtlasATT}(P,\eta)\) returns exactly that Corollary 1 aggregate ATT as a singleton. Their CS-LT condition bounds only conditional treatment assignment away from zero and one, whereas \(\mathcal M_\eta\) independently boxes every mixing, assignment, and transition primitive in \([\eta,1-\eta]\). The proved published-class comparison is equality of the ATT functional on the stated intersection; no inclusion of the full Ahn--Kasahara class in \(\mathcal M_\eta\), no inclusion of \(\mathcal M_\eta\) in their full class, and no completion theorem on their unboxed singular class is asserted. On this same regular intersection, within-arm recovery is exhaustive up to labels; hence the only candidate global alignments are the two relative permutations, and the singleton conclusion is equivalent to equality of their two feasible aggregate ATT vectors.
statements.justification: This intersection theorem certifies estimand fidelity without presenting the compact singular-completion theorem as an extension of the published model class.
statements.gap: Ahn--Kasahara Proposition 4 and Proposition 5 plus Corollary 1 establish regular identification under RSM, M, TI-LT, and ID. The proposed result complements those regular theorems by classifying singular fibers only inside the independently compactified \(\mathcal M_\eta\); a comparison on the unboxed published singular class is not claimed.
statements.consumer: The \(ak\) package can verify agreement on laws satisfying both sets of hypotheses while labeling boxed singular-set output as a separate analysis.

statements.statement: Under independent multinomial sampling, \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_\eta}P^n\{\mathcal I(P)\subseteq\mathcal C_n^\tau\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(n\ge1\). The infimum is over the independently stated model \(\mathcal M_\eta\), which boxes every mixing, conditional treatment-assignment, and transition primitive in \([\eta,1-\eta]\); it is not a coverage claim for the full Ahn--Kasahara class under CS-LT. The same event covers both marginal sets simultaneously and preserves their finite-union structure.
statements.justification: The confidence object covers every observationally compatible ATT value uniformly on the stated compact all-primitive class without selecting a latent branch.
statements.gap: Ahn--Kasahara's bootstrap uses regular point identification; general criterion methods do not exploit the exact multinomial fiber or guarantee preservation of disconnected components by this construction.
statements.consumer: Empirical reports can replace a misleading shrinking Wald interval by an honest confidence region for the entire merger set.

statements.statement: If \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta^{\mathrm{bc}}\), a nearest feasible law \(\widetilde P_n\in\arg\min_{Q\in\mathcal M_\eta}\lVert Q-\widehat P_n\rVert_\infty\) satisfies \(d_H(\mathcal I(\widetilde P_n),\mathcal I(P))\to_p0\), and every ordered marginal endpoint converges in probability. This Hausdorff and endpoint conclusion is not asserted for \(P\in\mathcal M_\eta\setminus\mathcal M_\eta^{\mathrm{bc}}\). Without branch lower persistence, there is a feasible sequence \(P_n\to P\) for which fixed-coverage plug-in Hausdorff consistency fails, even though outer excess remains controlled by compactness.
statements.justification: It separates honest coverage on the compact model from topology-sensitive endpoint and Hausdorff recovery, which is conditional on \(\mathrm{BC}(P)\).
statements.gap: Random-set and criterion-inversion theory does not identify the transition-model branch persistence needed for this Hausdorff conclusion.
statements.consumer: Software can state when estimated merger endpoints are stable and warn when a branch contact invalidates a fixed-coverage consistency claim.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under RSM, M, and ID, Proposition 4 identifies the parameter vector; adding TI-LT, Proposition 5 identifies LTATT and Corollary 1 identifies aggregate ATT; CS-LT bounds conditional treatment assignment away from zero and one.
Theorem 1 identifies one finite Markov mixture from four consecutive observations under three separation conditions, up to a common type permutation.
The paper supplies a birational inverse and semialgebraic membership procedure for a single binary hidden Markov model, with denominator-zero cases assigned to lower-dimensional submodels.
Kruskal-based tensor arguments establish generic identifiability of several latent-structure models outside an exceptional parameter set.
The paper characterizes finite-mixture identified sets under an excluded source of mixture-weight variation using probability and monotonicity restrictions.
The algorithm reduces discrete causal bounds to polynomial optimization and provides certified \(\epsilon\)-sharp outer bounds through spatial branch-and-bound.
Under a nondegeneracy condition and the stated state-count restriction, exact length-three trail probabilities recover the component Markov chains.
Monte Carlo profile-criterion confidence sets have uniform validity across classes containing point- and partially identified models, including selected singular cases.
With a Gaussian first-stage limit, ordinary bootstrap consistency for a transformed parameter is equivalent to full differentiability under the paper's regularity conditions.
Test inversion constructs confidence regions with pointwise and, under additional conditions, uniform coverage for criterion-defined identified sets and their images.
Random-set methods establish consistency and limit theory for a class of partially identified sets under their regularity conditions.

tldr: On the independently stated fixed compact-interior model \(\mathcal M_\eta\), a binary four-period latent-transition law can lose component identification exactly where an applied ATT sign is most fragile. The labeled fiber \(\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\) is reconstructed by sixteen lifted terminal-collision charts, its quotient \(\Phi_\eta(P)\) removes simultaneous type labels, and permutation invariance makes \(\bar\tau_P\) well defined on quotient classes. A finite observable necessity-and-sufficiency list handles both relative alignments when treated terminal rows are distinct and exactly one control terminal row collides; the open-ended question completes the remaining charts with a global all-chart constancy criterion. The result complements Ahn--Kasahara's regular identification results but does not claim to extend their full CS-LT class. For rational input, \(\mathsf{AtlasATT}\) has sixteen collision charts, \(81\) collision-orientation cells, and \(162\) relative-alignment base branches and returns exact attained finite-union regions, real-algebraic endpoints, and reconstructed latent witnesses. Whole-set coverage is uniform on \(\mathcal M_\eta\), while endpoint and Hausdorff consistency require \(\mathrm{BC}(P)\).

project_justification.gap: Ahn--Kasahara Proposition 4 identifies the parameter vector under RSM, M, and ID, while Proposition 5 and Corollary 1 identify LTATT and aggregate ATT under TI-LT; the nonsingular-matrix, distinct-eigenvalue, and alignment requirements in ID leave collision fibers outside those regular results. Their CS-LT condition bounds only conditional treatment assignment away from zero and one. The independently stated \(\mathcal M_\eta\) additionally boxes mixing and every transition primitive, and no comparison is claimed for the unboxed published singular class. Generic latent-mixture theory also leaves exceptional causal fibers unclassified.
project_justification.niche: Inside the fixed compact-interior model \(\mathcal M_\eta\), the economically relevant ATT can remain point identified after latent parameters cease to be recoverable, or can become a disconnected set because each arm is separately recoverable while their types admit several relative alignments.
project_justification.fill: A new-condition singular-completion theorem on the fixed compact-interior model \(\mathcal M_\eta\) separates the labeled fiber \(\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\) from its simultaneous-label quotient \(\Phi_\eta(P)\), proves ATT invariance on quotient classes, and reconstructs each labeled representation from a feasible point in one of sixteen lifted spaces \(\mathsf X_c\subset\mathbb R^{32}\times\mathbb R^8\). The one-collided-control-row theorem executes the first complete necessity-and-sufficiency classification; the global open question compares reconstructed ATT values over every feasible pair of charts. The independent compactification makes the sharp regions attained, the exact certificate finite, and uniform procedures well defined on one fixed domain.

related_work: Ahn and Kasahara's Proposition 4 identifies the parameter vector under Assumptions RSM, M, and ID; Proposition 5 adds TI-LT to identify LTATT, and Corollary 1 identifies aggregate ATT. Their CS-LT condition bounds only conditional treatment assignment away from zero and one. The independently stated model \(\mathcal M_\eta\) instead boxes every mixing, assignment, and transition primitive so that exact regions are attained, chart certification is finite, and uniform procedures share a fixed compact domain. The regular-reduction theorem proves only that, on laws satisfying both sets of hypotheses, \(\mathsf{AtlasATT}\) equals the Corollary 1 aggregate ATT. It proves neither class inclusion nor a completion of the unboxed Ahn--Kasahara singular class. The collision atlas therefore complements the published regular-ID theorem on a different maintained domain. Higgins and Jochmans inform the constructive recovery step for one separated finite Markov mixture and its common ordering. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes inform the generic-identifiability benchmark. Critch informs the rational-chart and semialgebraic-membership architecture for binary hidden Markov models but does not couple treatment arms or target a causal functional. Henry, Kitamura, and Salanie inform exact finite-mixture geometry under excluded weight variation. Duarte and coauthors inform polynomial optimization over discrete causal models, but their spatial routine gives numerical \(\epsilon\)-sharpness rather than the fixed-model exact branch inventory, finite-union encoding, and endpoint witnesses here. Chen, Christensen, and Tamer, Romano and Shaikh, Fang and Santos, and Beresteanu and Molinari inform the inference layer; none is presented as a theorem-level target.
technical_internal_limitation: The full singleton certificate remains open on the fourteen patterns outside the two one-collided-control-row charts. The executed early-kill list is finite but can be large because it retains signed principal subresultants for rank-zero and box-face contacts; reducing that list without losing necessity is not claimed. The binary theorem does not cover the multi-category ADA specification.
honest_scope: The labeled-to-quotient permutation invariance, the sixteen lifted-chart equations, the one-collided-control-row signed-subresultant classification, the exact merger benchmark, and the concentration-based coverage route are claims to prove rather than prior established facts. The compact box defining \(\mathcal M_\eta\) is a proposal-specific condition on every mixing, conditional treatment-assignment, and transition primitive; it is independently motivated by attainment, finite exact certification, and uniform procedures on one fixed domain. Ahn--Kasahara's CS-LT condition bounds only conditional treatment assignment away from zero and one. No inclusion in either direction between \(\mathcal M_\eta\) and their full maintained class is proved, and no result is asserted on their unboxed singular class. The sole published-class comparison is equality with their Corollary 1 aggregate ATT on the intersection satisfying RSM, M, TI-LT, and ID. The remaining principal open content is completion of the observable sign atlas on the fourteen collision patterns outside the early-kill pair. For rational input the exact algorithm has sixteen collision charts and \(162\) relative-alignment base branches, with rank failures retained through zero sign cells. At \(\eta=1/10\) the fully specified benchmark law must reproduce the two sign-crossing intervals in Theorem 5. Whole-set coverage is uniform over \(\mathcal M_\eta\), but endpoint and Hausdorff consistency are conditional on \(\mathrm{BC}(P)\); outside \(\mathcal M_\eta^{\mathrm{bc}}\) only outer-excess control is asserted, and fixed-coverage plug-in Hausdorff consistency can fail.

novelty_justification: Ahn--Kasahara Proposition 4 identifies the parameter vector under RSM, M, and ID, and Proposition 5 plus Corollary 1 identify LTATT and aggregate ATT under TI-LT on that regular model. Their CS-LT condition bounds only conditional treatment assignment away from zero and one. This project does not claim to extend their full class. It states the fixed compact-interior model \(\mathcal M_\eta\) independently, boxing every mixing, assignment, and transition primitive to guarantee attained exact regions, finite certificates, and a common domain for uniform procedures. The proved comparison is equality with the Corollary 1 ATT on the intersection satisfying RSM, M, TI-LT, and ID; class inclusion and an unboxed singular completion are not claimed. Critch's rational inverse and semialgebraic membership test for one binary hidden Markov process and Higgins--Jochmans's recovery of one separated Markov mixture inform the algebraic architecture but do not classify a coupled-arm causal functional at collisions. The kernel is the singular completion inside \(\mathcal M_\eta\): a complete labeled two-arm transition-alignment fiber with an explicit simultaneous-label quotient and invariant ATT map, an explicit necessity-and-sufficiency list for both alignments in the one-collided-control-row stratum, an open completion of the remaining charts, and an exact rational-input algorithm with sixteen collision patterns, \(162\) relative-alignment base branches, retained rank-zero sign cells, finite-union output, and real-algebraic witnesses.
